results.title: Cursor Alternatives (2026): We Tested 10 Tools and the $0 One Scored 95.0% on SWE-bench
results.content:
## 1. Superset: Best for Running Coding Agents in Parallel

Superset is a source available desktop workspace for running many coding agents at once. Each task gets an isolated Git worktree, branch, terminal, and environment, so Claude Code, Codex, opencode, Cursor Agent, or any other CLI agent can work on the same repository without overwriting another agent's changes. The app brings monitoring, diff review, previews, ports, and editor handoff into one place.

Verdict: The strongest Cursor alternative when the bottleneck is supervising several agents rather than replacing one editor. Superset separates concurrent tasks with worktrees and gives one review surface for the results. [...] The best Cursor alternative for running several coding agents at once is Superset. It gives each Claude Code, Codex, opencode, or other CLI agent an isolated Git worktree, then puts terminal sessions, diffs, previews, and review in one desktop workspace. For a free, open-source in-editor agent, Cline and Kilo Code only charge model inference.

Cursor Pro is $20/mo and includes $20 of model usage, then continues on usage-based billing, and the editor is a proprietary VS Code fork. We compared 10 alternatives on price, license, GitHub stars, editor support, and the model each one runs. Three 2026 shifts matter: Claude Code now defaults to Claude Opus 5 and Codex to GPT-5.6 Sol, Windsurf is now Devin Desktop (windsurf.com redirects to devin.ai), and Cursor acquired Continue.dev. [...] ## Quick Comparison: Cursor Alternatives at a Glance

Superset leads when the job is coordinating several coding agents in parallel. Four agents are free and open-source (Cline, opencode, Kilo Code, Aider): the extension or CLI costs nothing and you pay only for the model you run. The cheapest paid plans are GitHub Copilot and Zed at $10/mo.

results.title: Parallel Coding Agents: The Complete Guide | Superset
results.content:
Dedicated orchestration workspaces. Tools built around the fleet rather than the file: Superset, Conductor, Parallel Code, and others. Worktree-per-task by default, every session visible in one place, diffs reviewed centrally. Reach for this layer once you are running parallel agents most days, not once a month.

For a full comparison across all three layers, see Best AI Coding Tools and Agents.

## A reproducible isolation check

We checked this on September 23, 2026 with Git 2.52.0 in a temporary repository: two task branches changed the same line independently. The main checkout stayed unchanged. After merging the first branch, merging the second returned a conflict in `README.md`. No coding agent was involved in this check; it tests Git isolation, not agent performance. [...] ### Which coding agents work in parallel setups?

Any agent that runs in a terminal: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI, Aider, and custom scripts. Agent-agnostic orchestrators do not care which one you pick, and mixed fleets (different agents for different task types) are common. [...] At small scale, discipline and tmux can carry you. Past that, you want a surface that shows every session, its status, and its diff in one place.
